title: SDK regression goldens and diff-runner playbook
author: Riley Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a repeatable, review-gated process for creating, validating, and maintaining SDK regression goldens (snapshot outputs) and the accompanying diff-runner tooling used in CI and local development. It focuses on deterministic fixtures, token-level billing emulation, and a minimal, review-first golden update workflow to prevent silent regressions in behavior or billing semantics.

Goals:
- Provide high-signal regression coverage for client SDKs and example apps without relying on production endpoints.
- Make it safe and fast to run in CI by emulating runtime behavior (latency, tokenization, KV cache warmups) and per-token cost.
- Ensure golden updates are auditable and require cross-team review for behavioral or pricing-impacting changes.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: SDKs (Python/TS/Go), example microservices, code samples embedded in docs, and CI workflows.
- Non-goal: full fuzz testing of model outputs. This is snapshot-focused, not a comprehensive adversarial evaluation.

Prerequisites:
1) Local dev environment with Docker and Node or Python installed.
2) Access to the dev-only emulator image: docker.redwood-internal.io/dev/emulator:stable.
3) Golden storage (git LFS recommended) configured for the repository.
4) A named test fixture set (see naming convention below).

Naming convention:
- Fixtures: fixtures/<sdk>/<feature>/<short-desc>.json
  - Example: fixtures/python/chat/temperature-0.0-system-prompts.json
- Goldens: goldens/<sdk>/<feature>/<short-desc>.golden.json
  - Example: goldens/node/embeddings/search-vector-golden.json

Quickstart: create and validate a golden locally
1. Start the emulator (billing + behavior):
   docker run -p 8080:8080 \n     -e EMU_BILLING_MODE=tokenized \n     -e EMU_TOKEN_COST_USD=0.000002 \n     -e EMU_LATENCY_MS=5 \n     docker.redwood-internal.io/dev/emulator:stable

2. Create a fixture request file (fixtures/python/chat/sample-request.json):
   {
     "model": "redwood-7b-inference",
     "messages": [
       {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."},
       {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the following text: Redwood helps..."}
     ],
     "temperature": 0.0
   }

3. Run the SDK harness to record a golden:
   # Python example (uses sdk-test-harness CLI)
   sdk-test-harness --emulator http://localhost:8080 \n     record --fixture fixtures/python/chat/sample-request.json \n     --out goldens/python/chat/sample-request.golden.json

4. Validate the golden locally (diff-runner):
   sdk-test-harness --emulator http://localhost:8080 validate \n     --fixture fixtures/python/chat/sample-request.json \n     --golden goldens/python/chat/sample-request.golden.json \n     --threshold 0.02

Tooling and diff semantics:
- diff-runner computes three signals: token-delta, normalized-levenshtein, and structured-field-match. The validation command returns a combined score in the range [0.0, 1.0] where lower is closer to golden.
- Thresholds: default combined threshold is 0.03 for behavior-facing tests and 0.01 for pure deterministic fixtures (e.g., temperature=0.0).
- For embedding/regression tests, we also compute cosine-similarity on vectors and require similarity >= 0.995 for critical paths.
- Token-delta tracks absolute differences in token counts to catch billing regressions. Any token-delta > 3 tokens or token-cost delta > 0.5% triggers a billing-review label in CI.

Example golden (abbreviated):
{
  "meta": {"sdk": "python", "fixture": "chat/sample-request", "recorded_at": "2025-11-20T15:12:03Z"},
  "request": { ... },
  "response": {
    "choices": [
      {"message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "Redwood Inference is a platform…"}},
    ],
    "token_count": 46,
    "estimated_cost_usd": "0.000092"
  }
}

CI integration (GitHub Actions)
- Use a dedicated CI job with the emulator container and caching for golden files. The job must:
  1) Start emulator (see quickstart env vars)
  2) Run tests with --validate-only to avoid accidental golden writes
  3) If validation fails, produce a failure artifact with diffs and token-cost delta
  4) If the PR author intentionally updates a golden, require an Approval from owner_team and reviewer group before merging

Sample GitHub Action step (YAML snippet):
- name: Start emulator
  run: |
    docker run -d --name redwood-emulator -p 8080:8080 \n      -e EMU_BILLING_MODE=tokenized \n      -e EMU_TOKEN_COST_USD=0.000002 \n      docker.redwood-internal.io/dev/emulator:stable
- name: Validate goldens
  run: |
    sdk-test-harness --emulator http://localhost:8080 validate --all --report ./reports/golden-diffs.json || true
- name: Upload diff artifact
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: golden-diffs
    path: ./reports/golden-diffs.json

Golden update policy (approved updates only)
1) Small non-behavioral diffs (token-count only, < 1%) may be auto-approved by the SDK owner on a patch release.
2) Any behavioral change (normalized-levenshtein > 0.02) or token-cost change > 0.5% requires a reviewer approval label 'golden-review' from at least one member of the core SDK reviewers.
3) For changes that affect customer-facing billing, security, or policy, escalate to finance-legal or security and include a short PR description with the cost delta and a link to the evaluation harness.

Tolerance and flaky outputs
- If a fixture is inherently noisy (sampling temperature > 0.3 or streaming non-deterministic tool calls), mark the fixture as flaky by adding a 'flaky' metadata field and either:
  - Increase threshold to a pre-approved value, or
  - Switch to a structured assertion (e.g., presence of expected entities, JSON schema match) instead of full snapshot equality.

Emulator billing knobs and examples
- Environment variables supported:
  - EMU_BILLING_MODE: [tokenized|flat|none] (default tokenized)
  - EMU_TOKEN_COST_USD: decimal string (e.g. 0.000002)
  - EMU_LATENCY_MS: integer (ms) to inject per-request
  - EMU_QUOTA_RPS: integer to emulate rate limits

Example: emulate a high-latency, high-cost run:
  docker run -p 8080:8080 \n    -e EMU_BILLING_MODE=tokenized \n    -e EMU_TOKEN_COST_USD=0.00001 \n    -e EMU_LATENCY_MS=120 \n    docker.redwood-internal.io/dev/emulator:stable

Auditability and review flow
- Each golden update PR must include:
  - The failing diff report exported from the diff-runner.
  - A short rationale: behavior change, upstream model upgrade, or intentional prompt change.
  - If billing impact > 0.2% include an entry in the PR checklist: cost-impact, owner acknowledgement, and tagged finance contact.
- Labels to apply on PRs: golden-review, cost-impact, flaky-fixture, emulator-regression

Troubleshooting common failures
- Failure: small whitespace or punctuation diffs
  - Action: run diff-runner with --normalize-whitespace and revalidate.
- Failure: token delta spikes
  - Action: confirm tokenizer version in emulator matches runtime (EMU_TOKENIZER_VERSION). If mismatch, pin tokenizer or update emulator.
- Failure: timeout in CI job
  - Action: increase emulator healthcheck timeout and ensure emulator container has sufficient CPU shares.

Maintenance and housekeeping
- Rotate flaky fixtures quarterly: team assigned: devx-test-maintenance.
- Golden pruning: orphaned goldens (no fixture references) will be removed during a monthly job; owners are notified via CODEOWNERS review.

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience SDK test platform (team alias: #devx-sdk-tests).
- On-call reviewer list: Aisha Patel, Marco Ruiz.
- Escalation: customer-success for customer-impacting behavior, finance-legal for cost-related concerns.

Appendix: example commands summary
- Record: sdk-test-harness --emulator http://localhost:8080 record --fixture <path> --out <golden>
- Validate: sdk-test-harness --emulator http://localhost:8080 validate --fixture <path> --golden <path> --threshold <value>
- CI run (all): sdk-test-harness --emulator http://localhost:8080 validate --all --report ./reports/golden-diffs.json

If you have questions, ping the #devx-sdk-tests Slack channel or open a ticket in the devx backlog with tag 'goldens'.
